blocks.title: Functional group
blocks.text: A functional group is an atom or group of atoms, or a double or triple bond, that gives an organic compound its characteristic properties.

Functional groups strongly affect both physical and chemical properties. Methanol and ethanol are liquids while methane and ethane are gases, and alcohols have higher melting and boiling points than the corresponding alkanes, because the hydroxyl group (-OH) can form hydrogen bonds; alkanes have no such group. In the same way, lower alcohols, carboxylic acids, glucose and sucrose dissolve in polar solvents such as water because of their polar functional groups.

items: The polarity of the bonds in the group.
The bond order, i.e. the number of bonds (single, double or triple) in the group.

blocks.text: Alkanes and cycloalkanes have no functional group: they have no charges, no significant polarity and no double or triple bonds.

blocks.prompt: Why does ethanol have a much higher boiling point than ethane?
blocks.explanation: Its -OH group forms hydrogen bonds between molecules; ethane has no functional group and only weak forces between molecules.

items: Functional group: the part of a molecule that decides its properties.
-OH allows hydrogen bonding: higher boiling points and water solubility.
